lines: Noise-cancelling headphones make things quieter by adding more sound.
Tiny microphones on the outside constantly listen to the noise around you.
Then a chip builds a copy of that sound wave.

beats.label: noise
lines: But it plays the copy flipped upside down.
When the two waves meet, peaks fill valleys, and they cancel out.

beats.title: Works best on...
lines: It works best on steady sounds, like a plane's engine hum.
Sudden, random sounds like voices are much harder to predict.
So the quiet you hear isn't really silence.
It's two sounds cancelling each other out.

sources.claim: ANC uses microphones and anti-noise of opposite phase; destructive interference; best on steady sounds, worse on sudden ones

youtube.title: Noise-cancelling headphones add sound to make silence 🎧
youtube.description: How active noise cancelling really works: microphones, a flipped sound wave, and destructive interference.
